_comment: Data/Content/weeks/week-<n>/day-<n>.json - ONE day of the course, built by `npm run build:content` from the course package in Data/Source/course/. Never edit it by hand: edit the source and rebuild. A day has UP TO 4 parts, and nothing downstream may assume four.

day._comment: The day's position within its week, 1-5. The page's address uses it: /learn/w2/d1.

number._comment: The day's number across the whole course (Week 2 starts on Day 6). The lessons and their file names count this way, so the page shows it.

title._comment: The day's title, shown in the week menu and the course index.

locked._comment: true for a day that is written but not open yet. The UI shows it greyed and refuses to open it.

parts._comment: 1 to 4, in order. Each part is one tab of the day.

kind._comment: prerequisite = the Prerequisites section. concept = Fundamentals and Implementation. practice = Practice.

tab_label._comment: The text on the part's tab: the section's title.

has_runnable_code._comment: true when the part has code to open in the editor, commands to run, or code and terminal exercises. Drives the editor's empty state.

blocks._comment: Ordered content blocks, in DOCUMENT ORDER. Each lesson of a section is a `##` heading in a markdown block, followed by its blocks. markdown renders as prose (output samples are ```output fences); code is a sample with its file and command; terminal is commands, one per line, each with a Run button; callout is a boxed note; diagram is mermaid source; checkpoint is a quiz question; problem-ref marks where an exercise sits. at-a-glance opens the day.

text._comment: Markdown for markdown, callout, at-a-glance and recap; source code for code, example and your-turn; the commands, one per line, for terminal; mermaid source for diagram; markdown for reference; the question for checkpoint; the exercise number as a string for problem-ref.

starter._comment: your-turn ONLY: runnable code that 'Try it' loads. null for every other block type.

variation._comment: your-turn ONLY: the prompt the learner reads. null for every other block type.

checkpoint._comment: checkpoint ONLY. Formative and never scored - nothing is written to progress.

answers._comment: 0-based indexes into options: one for single and truefalse, one or more for multiple.

kind._comment: multiple asks the learner to select every correct option, then check.

explanation._comment: Shown after answering, right or wrong - the reason, not just the verdict.

code._comment: code ONLY: where the sample belongs and how it runs. null for every other block type.

file._comment: Path relative to the learner's project folder, such as tests/day1/auto-wait.spec.ts or ts-basics/day3/hello.ts. The Terminal saves the editor there. null for a snippet.

run._comment: The command that runs it, such as `node day3/hello.ts`. Run opens the sample in the editor as its file and runs this in the Terminal. null when there is none.

mode._comment: editor = can be opened in the editor; read = shown only.

expect_error._comment: The sample fails on purpose: a type error, or a failing test.

callout._comment: callout ONLY. The source's platform callouts are notes for the app's builders and are left out.

title._comment: reference ONLY: the title shown while the full table or list is collapsed. null for every other block type.

problems._comment: Present ONLY on a practice part: the day's exercises. The count is not fixed.

difficulty._comment: The exercise's level. null for an exercise that carries none.

kind._comment: code = written and run in the editor; terminal = commands; written = an answer in words; predict = shows code and asks what it does.

statement._comment: Markdown: what to build, where, and how you will know it worked.

stub._comment: What 'Start this in the editor' loads, for a code exercise only: its starter code, the code its prompt gives to fix, the file it says to copy, the lesson file it names, or a comment naming a new file. null for a written, predict or terminal exercise, and for a code exercise whose file the studio cannot run (such as playwright.config.ts); the button is then absent.

file._comment: A code exercise's file, relative to the learner's project folder.

run._comment: The command that runs a code exercise.

check._comment: How 'Check my answer' grades the exercise, from the course's own check. Kept only where the studio can grade the learner's code: a code exercise that opens in the editor. null for every other exercise, and the button is then absent.

kind._comment: stdoutEquals: the program's trimmed output must equal `expected`. testsPass: the command must succeed, so every test passed.

run._comment: The command the check runs, as a Terminal command.

solution._comment: Model answer in MARKDOWN, revealed on a deliberate click. A code answer that is the whole file loads into the editor as the exercise's file. null = not written, and the reveal button is absent rather than broken.

workspace._comment: The Terminal workspace the day's commands run in. 'demo' is ready-made with the day's own files, for a day before the learner has a project; 'project' is the learner's own project, which starts as `npm init playwright@latest` leaves it and keeps what they save.
